prompt: What happens when this program is compiled and run?
choices: It prints `hi` and then an empty string
A compile error: `a` was moved into `b`
A runtime crash when `a` is read
explain: `String` owns heap memory, so `let b = a;` moves ownership to `b` and `a` can no longer be used. Rust rejects this at compile time. Use `a.clone()` if you need two owners.
